subject: Private deployment addendum: operator access & audit evidence
messages:
From: Alex Khan <alex.khan@healthsync.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@healthsync.com, Priya Nair <cpo@healthsync.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment addendum (redlines)

Irene —

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. We reviewed the MSA and the Private Deployment addendum with Legal and Security. Attached is our consolidated redline (HealthSync_Redlines_PrivateAddendum.docx). High level items we care about:

- Operator access window: we want to limit any Redwood operator console access to scheduled maintenance windows and require pre-authorized SSO/temporary creds.
- Audit snapshots: request for periodic on-site or remote snapshot evidence of the deployed image and a short custody attestation.
- Code escrow / recovery path: if Redwood goes insolvent or can’t remediate, we need a defined escalation / escrow-like route (we suggested SecureVault as an escrow holder).
- Licensing: explicit language that the customer has a perpetual right to run the particular model release used at time of installation (for safety of operations).

Can you confirm who on Redwood will drive the technical evidence package (runbook, checksums, snapshot cadence), and who will own the legal redline review? Procurement would like an estimated timeline to finalize changes so we can align our procurement review.

Thanks,
Alex Khan
Legal — HealthSync Solutions

[Attachment: HealthSync_Redlines_PrivateAddendum.docx (docx, 128KB)]

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Khan <alex.khan@healthsync.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment addendum (redlines)

Alex — thanks for the clear redline and the list. Looping in Dev for the technical evidence and Connor for Dedicated/Private deployment policy. Marissa, would you take primary on legal coordination (we can stage changes: technical appendix + legal addendum)?

Quick answers:
- Operator access: we already support SAML short-lived operator sessions and have an audit log for operator actions; Dev can outline the maintenance window process and can propose an operator access playbook.
- Audit snapshots: we can provide periodic image hashes and an access window for remote snapshot verification; on-site evidence requests typically need 30 days notice and a scoped SOW.
- Escrow-like path: we can confirm a third-party neutral custodian for critical artifacts; we need to validate scope (operator tooling vs model binaries vs compiled runtime).
- License scope: we typically grant a perpetual binary run license for the pinned model bundle used in the deployment; legal to confirm wording.

Proposed next steps:
1) Dev to produce a 1-page "evidence package" summary and a short runbook (attachments) by Tue 2026-01-19.
2) Redwood legal (Marissa) to provide draft redline responses by Wed 2026-01-21.
3) If needed, schedule a 30-minute call next week to walk Procurement and Security through the evidence artifacts.

I will attach a short template for the runbook and a sample custody attestation we use for other customers.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: PrivateDeploy_Runbook_Summary.pdf (pdf, 42KB)]

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Alex Khan <alex.khan@healthsync.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment addendum (redlines)

Alex, Irene —

Thanks — I put together the evidence package stub below and attached the short runbook. High-level summary:

- What we can provide immediately:
  * Deployment manifest (sha256 of bundle), runtime version, and kernel/quantization profile used at deployment time.
  * Operator action logs (timestamped), limited to operator accounts.
  * Remote snapshot verification: we can provide transient, read-only access to the deployment image for a 72-hour window; we will timebox it and record access.

- Where we need clarification from HealthSync:
  * If you need physical on-site verification (full image forensics) vs remote checksum validation. On-site will trigger SOW and an approximate 30–45 day scheduling lead time.
  * Scope of what counts as "model artifacts" — do you need source model weights, quantized binaries, or only runtime bundles we ship? (We prefer defining the bundle we ship as the escrow artifact.)

- Proposed snapshot cadence: quarterly automatic bundle hashes + triggerable snapshot on major version changes.

Connor, is there any limitation from our Dedicated operations side on allowing SecureVault as an approved custodian?

Thanks,
Dev
Principal Software Engineer, Inference Runtime

[Attachment: PrivateDeploy_Runbook_Summary.pdf (pdf, 42KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Khan <alex.khan@healthsync.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment addendum (redlines)

Alex / team —

We reviewed the redlines and Dev’s evidence summary. A few legal points we will propose in the draft response:

1) Escrow-like custody: we can accept a third-party custodian for a narrowly defined set of artifacts: the compiled runtime bundle + deployment manifest and a text-based operator runbook. We will not include internal source code or internal orchestration tooling (we will instead provide a documented fallback procedure and an attestation of the bundle integrity).

2) Operator access: propose language that allows Redwood to perform emergency access with notice + post-hoc attestation, and routine access only during pre-scheduled maintenance windows with SSO and audit logging.

3) Evidence delivery / SOW: accept remote snapshot verification as the default; on-site forensics will be available on a time-and-materials SOW and with 30 days' notice.

4) License: propose language granting a perpetual, non-exclusive binary run license for the specific bundle shipped at deployment date; include a clause for model upgrade paths and a defined rollback process.

I'll circulate the draft redline (tracked changes) by EOD Wed 2026-01-21 and include markups for the addendum and a suggested escrow custodian clause. If HealthSync prefers SecureVault specifically, please share their contact/team so we can run our standard custodian validation questionnaire.

If helpful, I can join a 30-minute call Thurs 2026-01-22 at 11:00 PT to go through the legal language.

—Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
